predecessors.name: Mughal Empire
predecessors.text: the Mughal Carnatic subah ('Mughal subah 1692-1710', seat Arcot), independent from 1710

successors.name: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)
successors.text: the Carnatic region 'brought under British rule' by the Carnatic Treaty: the districts of North Arcot, South Arcot, Nellore, Trichinopoly, Madura and Tinnevelly were created in 1801

ledger.x: 1710: the Carnatic becomes an independent state under Saadatullah Khan I at Arcot.
1710: the court moves from Gingee to Arcot (infobox 'Arcot 1710-1768').
1734: the Nawab's expedition goes south against Madurai.
14 March 1741: Trichinopoly surrenders to Raghuji Bhonsle (Maratha Empire page).
1776: Thuljaji is reinstated 'on condition of hosting a British subsidiary garrison'.
26 July 1801: the Nawab Azim-ud-Daula signs the Carnatic Treaty, 'ceding tax rights to the British'.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

wars.name: Carnatic-Madurai war (conquest of the Madurai Nayak kingdom)
wars.outcome: The Nawab's expedition of 1734 and the rebellion of Chanda Sahib ended the Madurai Nayakas in 1736 (infobox 'Disestablished: 1736'); the Carnatic annexed Madurai.

wars.name: Maratha invasion of the Carnatic
wars.outcome: Dost Ali Khan was killed at Damalcherry in 1740 and Arcot surrendered; Trichinopoly surrendered on 14 March 1741.

wars.name: Carnatic Wars
wars.outcome: The French took Madras on 21 September 1746 and returned it in 1748; Clive took Arcot in 1751 (siege of Arcot 23 September - 14 November 1751); the Treaty of Pondicherry (1754) recognised Muhammad Ali Khan Wallajah as Nawab; Wandiwash 1760, Pondicherry 1761…

wars.name: Occupation of Thanjavur by the Nawab and the Company
wars.outcome: Thanjavur was occupied in 1773 and Thuljaji deposed; he was reinstated in 1776 with a British subsidiary garrison.

certainty.note: The pages give a province 'from the Krishna River to the Kaveri River' but no boundary; the southern limit after 1736 is Cliopatria's.
